applies_why: The judge text weighs a link ('Acts 2:30') by setting the challenger's own seed/loins chain against the defender's chain, which is the chain-against-chain collision the rule governs.
quote: the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires
room: The phrase 'does not name Joseph as the begetter' could be read as a neutral description of what the chain's footing covers, or as a stating-verse objection (no verse in the chain states the contrary in its own words); I weighed both and took the second, since the rule retires exactly that kind of test.
why: The judge discounts the challenger's chain for lacking an explicit naming of Joseph, which is the stating-verse test the rule retires, rather than weighing the two chains only by footing.
